Bnamericas Published: Thursday, October 01, 2026

Japan's SoftBank Group (SBG) completed its acquisition of US-based DigitalBridge, an alternative asset manager focused on digital infrastructure, for about US$3.1 billion, the Japanese group announced.

With that, DigitalBridge becomes a controlled subsidiary of SBG but will continue to operate as a separately managed platform, led by Marc Ganzi. The deal closed on September 30. DigitalBridge's financial position and results will be included in SBG's consolidated financial statements from that date, SoftBank sid.

Under the deal signed in December 2025, SoftBank agreed to pay US$16.00 per share in cash, in a transaction with a total enterprise value of about US$4bn. DigitalBridge had fee-earning equity under management of US$40.2bn as of June 30.

SoftBank announced the deal as part of its global AI push and the transaction also comes amid heated investment and M&A activity in the digital infrastructure landscape.

In July, a consortium of the Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Partnership (AIP), MGX and BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) completed the acquisition of Aligned Data Centers, in a transaction that valued the US company at about US$40bn, one of the largest private investments in the sector.

Aligned controls Odata, one of Scala's competitors in Latin America's hyperscale data center market, and the consortium committed an additional US$5bn in growth capital for Aligned's expansion.

In Latin America, DigitalBridge's portfolio includes Scala Data Centers, which operates hyperscale facilities in Brazil, Mexico and Chile; Highline do Brasil, a wireless infrastructure provider; fiber operator Mundo in Chile; Mexico Telecom Partners (MTP), which owns private towers in Mexico; and Andean Tower Partners (ATP), with towers in Colombia, Peru and Chile.

Its main regional portfolio company, Scala operates 13 data centers in Latin America and obtained authorization in September from power regulator Aneel for the grid connection of its signature Scala AI City project in Eldorado do Sul, in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul state.

CEO Marcos Peigo told BNamericas at the time that the company expected grid operator ONS's access opinion for 1.8GW within weeks. The project's first phase, of around 50MW, requires initial investment of R$2.6bn (US$500 million), with construction expected to begin in 2027.

As disclosed by BNamericas, IDB Invest is also weighing a US$300mn loan to Scala to finance the expansion of its portfolio in Brazil, as part of a senior asset-backed financing of around US$1.09bn with a five-year tenor. If approved, it would be IDB Invest's first financing for the data center sector in Latin America.

Highline, which has around 5,900 sites in Brazil and is controlled by DigitalBridge alongside Allianz, Rosewood, IFC and Alberta Investment Management Corporation, is expected to cut investment to reduce leverage.

Without capital injection from DigitalBridge, its capex should fall to around R$65mn (US$12.5mn) in 2027 from about R$230mn this year, according to Fitch's projections.

Mundo, Chile's second-largest fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) broadband provider with a 24.8% market share, was awarded a last-mile fiber project in August to connect 33 rural localities in the Aysén region.

The project is worth 7.68bn pesos (about US$8.4mn) and is fully funded by the regional government. In April, the company issued a US$435mn sustainable senior bond backed by DigitalBridge, with the participation of Goldman Sachs, Scotiabank, Santander and Brazil's BTG Pactual.

SoftBank's Vision Fund is also a investor at DayOne Data, whose executives met with Argentine President Javier Milei in September to discuss potential investments in the country.

This company is headquartered in Singapore and operates data centers in Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain.

SoftBank is also a founding partner of the Stargate AI infrastructure project in the US - whose potential Argentine leg was announced in October 2025, when OpenAI and Sur Energy signed a letter of intent to explore developing a data center of up to 500MW in the country.

(The original version of this content was written in English)
